topic: The Mystery of π in the Normal Distribution: The Gaussian Integral

sections.title: The Hook: The Gaussian Bell Curve
lecture_lines: Look at the standard normal curve.
Why is π in linear distributions?
animations: Highlight the standard normal curve on the screen.
Display the mathematical function formula on screen.
Show a question mark next to the π term [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Normalization Condition
lecture_lines: Probability requires area to be one.
animations: Highlight the area under the curve to represent probability.
Display the integral equation on the center-right.
Label the integral expression as I.

sections.title: The Mathematical Trick: Squaring the Integral
lecture_lines: To solve I, we square it.
animations: Square the integral I on the screen.
Display the multiplication of two integrals as volume.
Visualize the 2D surface representing the product using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/surface.svg].

sections.title: The Polar Coordinate Transformation
lecture_lines: Switch from rectangular to polar coordinates.
The variables shift to r and θ.
animations: Animate transition from x,y to r,θ using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/compass.svg] for orientation.
Draw a polar grid overlay in #66FF66 with a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/protractor.svg] to represent the angular measurement.
Display the change of variables formula clearly.

sections.title: Solving and Synthesis
lecture_lines: I equals the square root of π.
animations: Display the integral over polar coordinates r and θ.
Show the emergence of the 2π term in the result.
Display the final result that I equals sqrt(π).
